records.title: Study of Bends: A Comparison in Low Pressure Chamber and Actual Flight
records.author: Tobias CA, Lyons WR, Williams OL, Bridge EV, Lawrence JH, Helmholz HF Jr, Sweeney AR Jr

observations.outcome_window: During the 35,000-ft actual B-24 flights, up to 75 minutes at altitude or symptom-related early termination.
observations.note: Figure 2 prints 19 passed and 17 failed among the 36 actual subject man-runs. This is an earlier margin with different selection from the 1945 Table II comparison. The chamber-to-flight cross-classification is unclear in the text-only figure. The separate 10/72 aircrew bends margin is already extracted under Lawrence.
observations.protocol: Two matched chamber runs per subject. Aircraft ascent averaged 54 minutes. Subjects began oxygen at 15,000 ft and step-up exercise at 25,000 ft.

observations.outcome_window: Surveillance dates and ascertainment window are unavailable.
observations.note: The same extract gives fewer than 100 serious reactions. Five fatalities are a reported aggregate, with uncertain overlap with published individual cases.
observations.protocol: Broad wartime tally. Masland labels the denominator chamber flights. Individual and session linkage are unavailable.

fatality_crosswalk.note: Fryer cites this report under case 1. Onset, signs during decompression, and terminal autopsy findings agree. Fryer tabulates 8.5 h with a different or unclear clock.
Shared wrist onset at 35 min, BP 100/60, pulse 60, sweating, progressive right hemiparesis and peak hematocrit 65. Fryer gives age 26, 38,000 ft and 71 h. Retain both source profiles.

additional_nonfatal_chamber_narrative.symptoms: Right hemiplegia and hemianesthesia on descent
additional_nonfatal_chamber_narrative.catalogue_overlap: Unresolved. No additional case is counted.
